title: Introduce frag-rescue-oracle and SSE ordering-preserver to recover mid-frame JSON and maintain event ordering
author: Ava Mitchell
description: Context: We continue to see customer-reported and synthetic failures where SSE streams emit partial JSON spans due to chunk boundaries cutting UTF-8 characters or JSON tokens. Symptoms included: malformed JSON in the client, tool/function-call events being applied out of order, and duplicate function-call handoffs when a reconnect replay drove overlapping fragments. This PR introduces two coordinated components to make the streaming surface more resilient without changing the public API: 1) frag-rescue-oracle: a lightweight reassembly heuristic that maintains ephemeral fragment metadata (short rolling checksums, token-boundary flags, and windowed offset hints) to resynchronize mid-frame JSON without waiting for full checkpointed frames. It opportunistically repairs partial UTF-8 and JSON token splits, tries minimal escape/unescape correction, and emits a repair-confidence header for downstream callers. 2) ordering-preserver: a scheduler-level guard that assigns monotonic event ordinals and provides an idempotent replayer for late-arriving fragments so tool/function call events retain logical ordering across reconnects and buffered replay. Motivation: previous fixes focused on delimiter normalization and checkpoint anchors; gaps remained when split boundaries coincide with UTF-8 multi-byte sequences or when clients replay partial windows concurrently. The approach here is conservative: prefer emitting recoverable JSON (with repair header) over dropping events or blocking the stream. Backwards compatibility: OpenAI SSE compatibility adapter is updated to translate the repair headers into compatibility-safe event annotations (no new required fields). Implementation notes: - frag-rescue-oracle implemented in server/streaming/frag_rescue.rs; it exposes a compact API used by the SSE parser and the stream coordinator. - sse_parser was refactored to consult the oracle before deciding to flush a partial JSON buffer. - ordering-preserver lives in server/streaming/order_preserver.rs and hooks into the stream coordinator; it adds an ordinal to each logical event and persists a tiny checkpoint in memory for reconnect windows. - openai_compat adapter maps existing "delta"/"event" names to preserve ordering semantics for OpenAI-compatible clients (no surface change in the REST API). - observability: new metrics (stream_frag_repaired_total, stream_repair_confidence_histogram, stream_event_ordinal_skew) and a dashboard doc updated. Testing: added deterministic unit tests for mid-utf8-splits and property tests for idempotent replay; integration harness includes a replay scenario that used to produce out-of-order function calls. Checklist: - [x] Design doc review with infra and SDK teams - [x] Unit tests for parser + rescue heuristics - [x] Integration replay scenario - [x] OpenAI compatibility adapter change request approved - [x] Added metrics and short Grafana panel - [x] Smoke-tested with hosted API in staging Notes on risk: The oracle is intentionally tuned to avoid speculative repairs for low-confidence cases; in those cases the parser falls back to the previous behavior (emit as-is and rely on existing checkpoint/resume). The repair-confidence header lets SDKs and clients decide whether to accept repaired JSON. Rollout plan: gradual rollout behind runtime feature flag (sse_frag_rescue=true) for 10% of traffic for two days, monitor stream_frag_repaired_total and downstream parsing errors. If metrics look good, increase to 100% and flip default. Related: several previous delimiter/anchor PRs but this one focuses on repair heuristics and ordering guarantees for replay windows.

diff_snippets: server/streaming/frag_rescue.rs: added FragRescueOracle struct with rolling_checksum() and attempt_repair(buffer) -> (repaired_buffer, confidence)
server/streaming/sse_parser.rs: before flushing, consult oracle.attempt_repair(buffer); if confidence>0.6 set repaired payload + add header 'x-sse-repair-confidence'
openai_compat/sse_adapter.go: translate repair header to event 'repair.notice' when client requests compatibility mode
server/streaming/order_preserver.rs: OrdinalAllocator with atomic counter and Replayer that de-dupes by (stream_id, ordinal, fragment_id)

release_notes: Fixes for partial-JSON emissions and out-of-order function/toolcall events when SSE chunk boundaries split tokens or UTF-8 sequences. Introduces a non-breaking repair header for clients to detect repaired payloads, and instrumentation to monitor repair confidence and event ordinal skew. Rollout via feature flag; no API contract changes.
notes_for_backport: Not required for patch release; this is a coordinated runtime change that depends on metrics and staged rollout. If backporting to release branches, also port the metrics registry change and the openai_compat adapter mapping.
